:::{#thm-matrix-map-linear}
#### Multiplying by a matrix is a linear map

For any $m \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$,
the function $f: \reals^p \to \reals^m$ defined by $f(\vx) = \matr{A}\vx$
is a linear map (@def-linear-map).

:::

::: proof

Both conditions are checked one entry at a time.
For each $i \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$, additivity:

$$
\ba
\paren{\matr{A}(\vx + \vy)}_i
&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij} (\vx + \vy)_j
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij} (x_j + y_j)
&& \text{(@def-vector-addition)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} (a_{ij} x_j + a_{ij} y_j)
&& \text{(multiplication distributes over addition)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij} x_j + \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij} y_j
&& \text{(a sum of sums splits)}
\\&= (\matr{A}\vx)_i + (\matr{A}\vy)_i
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\&= (\matr{A}\vx + \matr{A}\vy)_i
&& \text{(@def-vector-addition)}
\ea
$$

and homogeneity:

$$
\ba
\paren{\matr{A}(c\vx)}_i
&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij} (c\vx)_j
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij}\, c\, x_j
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} c\, a_{ij} x_j
&& \text{(products are symmetric)}
\\&= c \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij} x_j
&& \text{(a constant factor comes out of a sum)}
\\&= c\, (\matr{A}\vx)_i
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\&= (c\, \matr{A}\vx)_i
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult)}
\ea
$$

The four algebra rules cited here are on the [algebra page](algebra.qmd):
[distributivity](algebra.qmd#thm-mult-distr),
[a sum of sums](algebra.qmd#thm-sum-of-sums),
[symmetry of products](algebra.qmd#thm-prod-symmetric),
and [a constant factor](algebra.qmd#thm-sum-constant-factor).

:::
